items.actClause: AN ACT authorizing the city of New Rochelle to sell and convey certain lands in the city of New Rochelle
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S8307

TITLE OF BILL:
An act authorizing the city of New Rochelle to sell and convey certain
lands in the city of New Rochelle

PURPOSE:
To allow the City of New Rochelle to convey a parcel of land for the
purpose of facilitating economic development within the city.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
To allow the City of New Rochelle to sell, alienate and and convey the
parcel identified in Section 3 to further the economic development of
the waterfront.

Section 2: Provides the specific section, block and lot numbers of the
referenced parcel.

Section 3: Provides a metes and bounds description of the parcel.

Section 4: Authorizes the Commissioner of General Services to take
action as may be necessary to release, extinguish and relinquish
forever any state limits and rights to revertor and/or reversion for
the property.

Section 5: Establishes that the act shall take effect immediately.

JUSTIFICATION:
HOME RULE REQUEST - The City of New Rochelle has requested that
legislative authority be granted to the city regarding the
aforementioned parcel in order to advance plans to develop the
waterfront, a proposed mixed use project of residential, retail and
recreational uses. The parcel in question was conveyed by the state to
the city over a decade ago with restrictions attached or implied.  As
a matter of home rule, city officials request the full authority to
convey the property as may be needed to complete the waterfront
project. Any ultimate action taken by the city on this site would be
subject to existing laws mandating proper public notice, public
hearing, SEQR procedures and other public protections to ensure
community involvement prior to any final decision.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
New Bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None to the State. Future revenue generated in state taxes is
anticipated once the development is complete.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

summary: Authorizes the city of New Rochelle to sell, alienate and convey waterfront real property.
